reflections.title: God Will Be with You

reflect.text: As Jacob neared the end of his life, Joseph hurried to his bedside with his two sons. Long years of grief had once led Jacob to believe his joy was gone forever. Yet God was quietly working behind the scenes for good. In the end, the Lord gave Jacob far more than he ever expected, restoring his lost son and allowing him to hold his grandsons in his arms.

From his bed, the aged father used his remaining strength to shape the future of his family. By adopting Ephraim and Manasseh to share in the inheritance and placing his hands on them in blessing, Jacob left an enduring spiritual mark on the next generation. In the same way that Joseph was there to comfort his father, the Lord Jesus meets us in all our frailties and cares for us in both life and death.

Jacob knew his time on earth was closing, yet he could leave his family without fear because God would remain with them. When dear friends or relatives pass away, we can take comfort that the Lord never departs. His abiding presence gives us all the strength and safety we need for the road ahead.

questions: When you face seasons of sorrow or change, how does the promise of God's presence give you peace?
What faithful blessings and lessons about God can you pass along to the next generation?
reflections.prayer: Lord God, thank You for working for our good even when life seems painful and confusing. Thank You that You never leave us, but stay near in every trial and transition. Help us to rest in Your presence and share Your faithfulness with those coming after us. Amen.

D3.author: Meredith Houston Carr
D3.work: Believing God for Seasons of Joy Again
